questions.question: How should I split the work into tickets per repo?

options.label: One ticket per doc (Recommended)
options.description: ~7-9 tickets per repo (≈30 total). Each ticket = one MD file. Easy to parallelize across agents, easy to mark Done. Higher board volume.

options.label: One umbrella + per-doc subtasks
options.description: 1 umbrella ticket per repo with a checklist of sub-docs inside the body. ~4 board tickets total. Fewer tickets but harder to claim independently from parallel agents.

options.label: One ticket per repo, single big task
options.description: Just 4 tickets — 'create memory bank for X'. Minimal overhead but easy to underspecify and stall.

questions.question: Where should the docs live in each repo?

options.label: docs/ folder, AGENTS.md as root index (Recommended)
options.description: Matches the 2025/2026 AGENTS.md standard. CLAUDE.md stays as a thin pointer to AGENTS.md so both tool families work. ai-harness already on this layout.

options.label: .claude/memory/ folder
options.description: Co-located with Claude config. Cleaner separation of agent-only context vs human docs, but non-standard for non-Claude tools and less discoverable on GitHub.

options.label: memory-bank/ folder (Cline convention)
options.description: Matches Cline's named convention. Explicit but tool-specific; mixed signal if you're primarily on Claude Code.

questions.question: Should the plan include cross-cutting hygiene tickets to prevent doc drift?

options.label: Add a 'doc-sync checklist' to CONTRIBUTING / PR template
options.description: Per-repo ticket: add a 'docs updated?' checkbox to PR template + a one-liner in CONTRIBUTING.md.

options.label: Add a quarterly 'docs review' recurring schedule
options.description: Create a /schedule routine to re-review the memory bank quarterly per repo. Catches drift but adds recurring noise.

options.label: Skip drift guards for now
options.description: Just create the docs; revisit hygiene later.

## Research synthesis

Three patterns dominate the "memory bank in the repo" space:

- **AGENTS.md + docs/** (current 2025/2026 standard, co-promoted by OpenAI/Google/Anthropic/JetBrains): root-level `AGENTS.md` is the agent-facing entry point with build/test/style/setup commands; deep topics live in `docs/`.
- **Cline-style Memory Bank** (`projectbrief.md`, `productContext.md`, `systemPatterns.md`, `techContext.md`, `activeContext.md`, `progress.md`): great for AI continuity, but `activeContext` and `progress` are session-scoped — awkward to check in long-term.
- **arc42 / C4** (architecture-only, heavier): solid for the architecture doc itself, overkill as the whole structure.

Recommended hybrid: AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md) at root as an index + a curated `docs/` folder with stable, topical files. Avoids Cline's session-state drift problem and matches the de-facto standard.

## Current state across the four repos

- **dstrader** — Java/Maven. Has CLAUDE.md, README.md; lots of scattered topical MDs at root; `docs/` has only SECRETS/SETUP. Needs consolidation + new core docs.
- **dstrader-docker** — Compose orchestration. Has CLAUDE.md; `docs/` has only GPG_FIX and PRODUCTION_PAPER_DISCREPANCY. Architecture/ops largely undocumented.
- **FamilyFund** — Laravel. Most mature: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README.md, `docs/ENGINEERING_DECISIONS.md`, runbooks. Mainly needs *organization* (root MDs → `docs/`).
- **ai-harness** — Python tooling. Already has `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/OPERATIONS.md`, `DECISIONS.md`. Closest to done; just gaps and a skills index.

| `DEVELOPMENT.md` (setup, build, test) | new | new | reorg | new |
| `SECURITY.md` (secrets, SOPS+age, threat model) | reorg | new | reorg | new |
| `DOMAIN_GLOSSARY.md` | new (trading) | n/a | new (fund/accounting) | new (sessions/skills/hooks) |
| `INTEGRATIONS.md` (external systems) | new (IB/TWS, market data) | new (TWS, MariaDB, jump) | new (banks, dstrader) | new (Claude API, GitHub) |
